message.content:
Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are well‑known for offering vegetarian (and vegan) options:

| Restaurant | Location | Vegetarian Highlights | Notes |
|------------|----------|-----------------------|-------|
| **Baan Thai** | 1400 W. 18th St., West Loop | *Vegetarian Pad Thai*, *Vegetarian Green Curry*, *Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup* | Classic Thai dishes with a dedicated vegetarian menu; many dishes can be made vegetarian upon request. |
| **Siam Square** | 2000 N. Clark St., Near North Side | *Vegetarian Pad See Ew*, *Vegetarian Massaman Curry*, *Vegetarian Spring Rolls* | Offers a separate vegetarian menu; also has a vegan-friendly “Siam Square Vegan” option. |
| **Thai Orchid** | 4000 N. Lincoln Ave., Uptown | *Vegetarian Pad Krapow*, *Vegetarian Red Curry*, *Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Vegetables* | Known for generous portions and a dedicated vegetarian menu. |
| **Mango Tree** | 5000 N. Lincoln Ave., Uptown | *Vegetarian Pad Thai*, *Vegetarian Green Curry*, *Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Tofu* | Offers a separate vegetarian menu; many dishes can be customized. |
| **Siam Thai Bistro** | 3000 W. 18th St., West Loop | *Vegetarian Pad Thai*, *Vegetarian Massaman Curry*, *Vegetarian Spring Rolls* | Has a separate vegetarian menu; many dishes can be made vegetarian upon request. |
| **Siam Thai Kitchen** | 4000 N. Lincoln Ave., Uptown | *Vegetarian Pad Thai*, *Vegetarian Green Curry*, *Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Vegetables* | Offers a separate vegetarian menu; many dishes can be customized. |
| **Siam Thai Bistro** | 3000 W. 18th St., West Loop | *Vegetarian Pad Thai*, *Vegetarian Massaman Curry*, *Vegetarian Spring Rolls* | Has a separate vegetarian menu; many dishes can be made vegetarian upon request. |
| **Siam Thai Kitchen** | 4000 N. Lincoln Ave., Uptown | *Vegetarian Pad Thai*, *Vegetarian Green Curry*, *Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Vegetables* | Offers a separate vegetarian menu; many dishes can be customized. |

**How to choose:**

1. **Check the menu online** – Most of these restaurants have their menus posted on their websites or on food‑review sites like Yelp or Google Maps. Look for a dedicated vegetarian or vegan section.
2. **Call ahead** – If you’re planning a special meal or have dietary restrictions, it’s a good idea to call the restaurant and confirm that they can accommodate your needs.
3. **Ask for customization** – Even if a dish isn’t listed as vegetarian, many Thai restaurants can easily remove meat or fish and add tofu or extra vegetables.

Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago!
